sentences.l2: 清晨的菜市场门口，一位七十多岁的老人被拦在了门外。
sentences.l1: At the entrance of the vegetable market in the early morning, an old man in his seventies was stopped outside.

sentences.l2: 工作人员指着墙上的二维码，请他扫码进场。
sentences.l1: A staff member pointed at the QR code on the wall and asked him to scan the code to enter.

sentences.l2: 老人翻遍衣兜，只找到一张纸币和一部按键手机——屏幕小得看不清字，也装不了软件。
sentences.l1: The old man rummaged through his pockets and found only a banknote and a button phone, whose screen was so small that he could not make out the characters, and which could not install software either.

sentences.l2: 他看着年轻人举着手机一晃而过，觉得自己被隔在一层看不见的玻璃之外。
sentences.l1: He watched young people flash past holding their phones, and felt that he was cut off behind an invisible layer of glass.

sentences.l2: 疫情期间，健康码一度是出行的通行证；如今挂号、打车、缴费，越来越多的服务被搬进了智能手机的屏幕。
sentences.l1: During the epidemic, the health code was for a time the pass for going out; now, registering for appointments, hailing rides and paying bills, more and more services have been moved onto the screen of the smartphone.

sentences.l2: 技术在提升效率的同时，也悄然掘开了一道数字鸿沟：一端是熟练滑动屏幕的年轻人，另一端是不知从何下手的老人。
sentences.l1: While technology raises efficiency, it has also quietly dug a digital divide: on one end are young people who swipe the screen skillfully, and on the other end are old people who do not know where to start.

sentences.l2: 他们并非拒绝新事物，只是缺少学习的机会。
sentences.l1: They do not refuse new things; they just lack opportunities to learn.

sentences.l2: 真正的便利，不该以遗忘一部分人为代价。
sentences.l1: True convenience should not come at the cost of forgetting a part of the people.

sentences.l2: 保留人工窗口、把字体调大一些，或许才是让技术变得温和的开始。
sentences.l1: Keeping manual counters and making the font a bit larger may well be the beginning of making technology gentle.
